          WSL Matchday 5: The Opta Stats That Defined the Weekend
        
      
                          
                      Oct 5, 2026
          
                      Louise Bawden / Author, Maya Shah / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Arsenal’s difficult start continued, Man City and Chelsea stayed unbeaten and London City delivered the result of the weekend . Using Opta data, we uncover the standout performances, emerging trends and biggest numbers from Matchday 5 of the 2026-27 WSL season.
After five matchdays, there have already been 111 goals scored in the WSL – the second-most at this stage of the season behind just the 2020-21 campaign (115).

The opening weeks have seen league positions swap and change, but we head into the international break with Manchester City setting the pace. They have a perfect 15 points from 15, with Chelsea two points behind on 13 and highly anticipated newcomers London City Lionesses making their presence felt in third on 12 points.

The real story of these opening weeks, though, has arguably been Arsenal’s alarming start. The Gunners head into the international break down in 10th, with just five points from five games and back-to-back defeats leaving Renée Slegers under mounting pressure.
But, as ever, the results only tell part of the story. We’ve dug into the Opta data to uncover the standout performances, emerging trends and remarkable numbers that defined Matchday 5.
Arsenal’s alarming start to the season hit a new low on Sunday as they threw away a lead to lose 4-2 to Manchester City.

Having gone ahead, the Gunners were beaten in a WSL match for the first time since February 2024 against West Ham, ending a 37-game unbeaten run when scoring first and underlining the fragility that has defined their campaign.
There have not been many bright sparks during Arsenal’s difficult start, but summer signing Lisa Baum has provided a glimpse of what could be to come if they can turn things around.
The last younger player to do so was Ebony Salmon in November 2020, aged 19 years and 285 days.
In finding the net, Baum also helped Arsenal carve out a unique piece of WSL history.

For City, it was a very different story. They came from behind twice to beat Arsenal, securing their first WSL victory over the Gunners after conceding first since December 2020. In the five such meetings between those victories, City failed to win, drawing one and losing four.
It was also the fastest substitute goal in the competition since Pernille Harder against Everton in May 2023 (62 seconds).

Her leveller against the Gunners also meant the Dutchwoman also became the first defender in City’s WSL history to come off the bench and score a goal that either levelled the match or put City ahead.
City head into the international break with a perfect record and a growing sense of inevitability that whatever position they find themselves in, they can find a way to win.

Against Arsenal, Jeglertz's side generated just 1.01 xG to Arsenal's' 1.61, finishing the match with a -0.60 xG differential. It was the second-largest negative xG differential City have overcome in a WSL victory, and their first league win despite being second best on xG since a 2-1 victory over Brighton in March 2025 (-0.22).

With just one place separating the sides at kick-off, London City Lionesses seized the opportunity to overtake Tottenham in emphatic fashion. Spurs had begun the season in impressive form and sat second heading into the weekend, but a stunning 6-1 victory saw Eder Maestre's side move above them in the table.

They wasted little time taking control. Alexia Putellas’ third-minute opener was London City’s fastest WSL goal, while it was the earliest Tottenham have conceded in the league under Martin Ho, and their earliest since facing Arsenal in November 2024.

It means that Putellas has won 130 of the last 131 league matches in which she has scored, so once the ball hit the back of the net in the third minute, history suggested Spurs were already in trouble.

Diani was joined on the scoresheet twice by Putellas, with the pair making a little piece of WSL history in the process. It was the first time a French international and a Spanish international have both scored 2+ goals in the same WSL match.
For Tottenham, the scale of the defeat was particularly remarkable given their form coming into the game.
